body:
_Migrated from issue #1147, filed 2026-07-26._

Found while establishing the blast radius for #1144 (PR #1146).

## What is happening

Running `a11y.spec.ts` **twice against one unchanged build**, same container, same database, nothing edited in between:

```
run 1 — 4 failures
  grid, advanced-search, shelves, login (unauthenticated)

run 2 — 9 failures
  grid, advanced-search, shelves, book detail, edit book,
  smart shelf builder, account, admin, clickable announcement
```

Same build. Different answer. Across the wider work on #1144 the set moved again each time — one full-suite run had 7 a11y failures, another had 1.

## Why it matters

This is the gate that is supposed to hold the SPA at WCAG 2.2 AA, and its `KNOWN` list is deliberately empty so that any critical/serious violation fails the run. A gate that reports a different set each run cannot do that job in either direction: it cannot prove a change is clean, and it cannot be trusted when it goes red.

It also actively cost time here. The a11y cluster appeared in the post-fix run of an unrelated frontend change and had to be ruled out by hand — running the spec repeatedly to demonstrate non-determinism — before the one **real** regression in that run could be separated from the noise. That is the #1130 failure mode repeating: a permanently unreliable check trains people to skim past it, and the genuine finding underneath is what gets missed.

## What the violations actually are

Every one is `color-contrast [serious]` in the **light** theme, and the selectors are sidebar chrome, not the page under test:

```
_triggerLabel_1uzuf_157      1.22  (#ece8e1 on #ffffff)
_itemActive_110ti_20 > span  1.90  (#e6a13f on #f8eddf)
a[href$="authors"] > span    2.45  (#9aa7b2 on #ffffff)
_shelfName_110ti_94          2.45  (#9aa7b2 on #ffffff)
_sectionTitle_110ti_53       2.45  (#9aa7b2 on #ffffff)
_seg_2qoot_279               1.88  (#9aa7b2 on #e7e1d4)
```

So there are two separable problems, and they should not be conflated:

1. **The light theme has real sidebar contrast failures.** `#9aa7b2` on `#ffffff` is 2.45:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement. That is a genuine WCAG defect for anyone using the light theme, and it is not flaky — when a page's light sweep runs, it fails.
2. **Whether a given page's light sweep runs and fails at all is non-deterministic.** That is the part that makes the gate useless, and it is the reason failure #1 has been able to sit there unnoticed.

## Likely cause of the non-determinism

The harness already documents shared-account-state contention — `playwright.config.ts` excludes `default-library-view.spec.ts` from the mobile project with the note that specs "mutate ACCOUNT state ... every project shares one seed login, so running it here in parallel with desktop makes each project clobber the other's writes — a race, not a defect."

Theme is account state, `a11y.spec.ts` sweeps light and dark, and the suite runs `fullyParallel` with 6 workers. That is the shape of it, but it is a hypothesis and should be confirmed before anything is changed — the pages that flip are not a stable set, which does not obviously follow from theme alone.

## Suggested order of work

1. Confirm the mechanism (log the resolved theme per sweep; try `workers: 1` for this spec and see whether the set stabilises).
2. Make the spec own its theme rather than reading whatever the shared account currently has.
3. Once it is deterministic, fix the light-theme sidebar contrast properly — that is a real user-facing a11y defect and deserves its own change, not a `KNOWN` entry.

Related: #1130 (the SPA e2e suite being advisory and unread), #1144.
title: a11y.spec.ts reports a different failure set on every run, so the a11y gate cannot be trusted
